_howToEdit: This one file drives the Find Your Path quiz, the 'See the whole map' flowchart, and the question teaser on the homepage.
Each answer's 'goto' must match the 'id' of a question or a result in this file.
'mapLabel' is the short text shown in the flowchart. Keep it under about 40 characters.
After editing, rebuild the site (npm run build) or push to Netlify and it rebuilds for you.

meta.footnote: Based on Energize Denver small-building guidance as of {date}. The City makes the final eligibility determination.
meta.extensionText: Need more time? Extensions are available for situations like a pending sale, high vacancy, or budget approval cycles.

questions.text: Is your building between 5,000 and 24,999 sq ft?
questions.hint: Go by the total floor area of the whole building, not one unit or tenant space.

questions.text: Are at least 97% of your light fixtures already LED?
questions.hint: Count every fixture: inside, outside, and in parking areas.
questions.mapLabel: At least 97% of fixtures already LED?

questions.hint: If only part of the building is a restaurant, choose Not sure.

questions.text: Is it a condo building with shared common spaces?
questions.hint: Common spaces are areas like lobbies, hallways, laundry rooms, and parking.
questions.mapLabel: Condo building with shared common spaces?

questions.text: Do you have a gas furnace or rooftop unit near the end of its life?
questions.hint: If it's old, unreliable, or due for replacement soon, answer Yes.
questions.mapLabel: Gas furnace or rooftop unit near the end of its life?

results.title: You're okay.
body: Energize Denver's requirements start at 5,000 sq ft, so they don't apply to a building this size.
The City goes by the square footage in its own records. If your building is close to 5,000 sq ft, it's worth confirming the number on file.
handle: Look up your building in the City's records
Confirm the square footage on file

results.title: Larger buildings follow different rules. Let's talk.
body: Buildings 25,000 sq ft and larger report their energy use to the City every year and work toward an energy target.
The options on this page are for small buildings, so the plan for yours will look different. Tell us about the building and we'll talk it through.
handle: Look up where your building stands with the City
Talk through what the rules mean for your building

results.title: We'll look it up for you.
results.mapLabel: We'll look it up for you
body: The City keeps a record of every covered building, including its square footage and deadline.
Give us the address and we'll check what's on file.
handle: Find your building in the City's records
Confirm its size, deadline, and current status
Tell you which of these questions apply to you

results.title: You may already comply.
body: If at least 97% of your fixtures are LED, your building may already meet the lighting requirement.
The City still needs to see it documented. We verify it and file the paperwork.
handle: Count and document every fixture
Complete the City's lighting verification
File it with the City and send you a copy

results.title: Restaurant option
body: Restaurants have their own way to comply.

Replace one gas kitchen appliance (fryer, griddle, combination or convection oven, steam cooker, or the kitchen water heater) with an electric one, or complete the City's restaurant efficiency checklist.
We look at your kitchen and tell you which is simpler.
handle: Review your kitchen equipment
Install the electric replacement through licensed, insured contractors
Document the work and file it with the City

results.title: Condo option
body: Condo buildings can comply through their shared spaces.
That means 100% LED lighting in common areas (lobbies, halls, laundry, parking, exterior, exit signs), plus occupancy sensors where code allows.
handle: Survey every common-area fixture
Install LED fixtures and sensors through licensed, insured contractors
Complete the verification and file it with the City

results.title: Electrification option
body: Replacing one gas furnace or rooftop unit with a heat pump is one way to comply.
We also compare it against an LED retrofit and recommend the cheaper path.
handle: Inspect the heating equipment and the lighting
Price both paths and recommend the cheaper one
Manage the installation through licensed, insured contractors
File the paperwork with the City

results.title: LED option
body: Upgrade the lighting until at least 97% of fixtures are LED.
We use new fixtures or retrofit kits, not plug-in tubes in old ballasts.
handle: Count every fixture and plan the upgrade
Install new fixtures or retrofit kits through licensed, insured contractors
Verify the result and file it with the City

results.title: That's what the site walk is for.
results.mapLabel: That's what the site walk is for
body: You don't need to know the answer. We walk the building, count the fixtures, and look at the heating and kitchen equipment.
Then we tell you which path fits and what it takes.
handle: Walk the building and document what's there
Check it against the City's requirements
Recommend the path that fits
